```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# all paths below are relative to the project root
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

# set to FALSE to re-render text and plots from existing results only
run_pipeline <- TRUE
```

This vignette runs the Proteome part of the analysis pipeline on a small example
dataset that is included in the repository, reproduces the marker profile plot
of Figure 3c and builds a ranked table of candidate protein redistributions.

Rendering it runs the complete Proteome pipeline (`01` to `06`) and takes
roughly 15–30 minutes. To render it, start R in the project root and run:

```r
rmarkdown::render("vignettes/example_workflow.Rmd")
```

To re-render only the text and plots from existing results, set
`run_pipeline <- FALSE` in the first chunk of this file.

## Example dataset

`example_data/input/` contains a subset of the Spectronaut protein group report
used in the manuscript (PRIDE PXD067608):

- all proteins of the subcellular marker set (`Subcell_markers_selected.csv`)
  that were identified (639 of 650 marker entries), plus
- 500 randomly selected other proteins,
- for all 96 runs: 6 fractions × 4 conditions (`CTRL`, `Anis`, `p38`, `Zaki`;
  treatments as described in the manuscript) × 4 replicates.

All conditions and fractions are kept, because normalisation, imputation and
the limma contrasts are computed per fraction across all conditions. The report
is stored gzipped; `script/Proteome/00_path_definitions.R` uses the `.tsv.gz`
file when no uncompressed report is present.

```{r packages}
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r data-overview}
report <- readr::read_tsv(
  list.files("example_data/input/Proteome", pattern = "\\.tsv\\.gz$", full.names = TRUE),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

report %>%
  summarise(
    proteins = n_distinct(PG.ProteinGroups),
    runs     = n_distinct(R.FileName),
    rows     = n()
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

## Run the pipeline

The input and output folders are set with environment variables, which are read
by `script/Proteome/00_path_definitions.R`. Results are written to
`example_data/results/`, so the results of the full dataset in `data/` are not
touched.

```{r folders}
Sys.setenv(
  SUB001_RAW_DIR  = "example_data/input",
  SUB001_DATA_DIR = "example_data/results"
)
```

`run_pipeline.R` runs each script in its own R session, exactly as it would be
run on its own. `core` runs only the scripts that produce result tables (no QC
and figure scripts). The console output of every script is written to
`logs/proteome/`.

```{r run-pipeline, eval = run_pipeline}
rscript <- file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript")
status  <- system2(rscript, c("run_pipeline.R", "proteome", "core"))
stopifnot(status == 0)
```

## Marker profiles (Figure 3c)

`script/Proteome/04_8_...RepSep_centroids.R` plots the scaled intensity profiles
of the marker proteins across the six fractions (CTRL, per replicate, with the
centroid of each compartment). It is run here directly so that the plot is
shown in this document. When the script is run on its own (Rscript or
RStudio), it also saves the plot as a PDF in `<data folder>/Proteome/Plots/`.

```{r fig3c, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 8}
fig_env <- new.env()
source(
  "script/Proteome/04_8_scaled_intensity_profile_plots_selected_markers_nonimputed_RepSep_centroids.R",
  local = fig_env
)
fig_env$combined_plot
```

Because the marker profiles are computed per protein, they are expected to look
very similar to Figure 3c of the manuscript.

## Ranked candidate redistributions

`06_0_diff_and_scaled_mobility_top_movements_median.csv` contains one row per
protein, treatment and redistribution between two fractions, with the limma interaction
result (`diff`, `pval`, `adj_pval`) and the scores computed from the scaled
intensities:

- `median_pair_mobility_score`: share of the protein signal shifted between the
  two fractions of the redistribution (median of the replicates),
- `median_mobility_score`: overall redistribution of the protein across all
  fractions it was detected in.

Candidates are first selected by the adjusted p-value of the interaction
contrast and then ranked by the pair mobility score:

```{r candidates}
redistributions <- readr::read_csv(
  "example_data/results/Proteome/06_0_diff_and_scaled_mobility_top_movements_median.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

candidates <- redistributions %>%
  filter(adj_pval < 0.05) %>%
  arrange(desc(median_pair_mobility_score))

candidates %>%
  count(treatment, name = "significant redistributions") %>%
  knitr::kable()

candidates %>%
  select(pg_genes, treatment, movement, classified_movement, diff, adj_pval,
         median_pair_mobility_score, median_mobility_score) %>%
  head(20) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

## Differences to the full dataset

The candidate table above is not expected to match the results of the full
dataset exactly:

- **Multiple testing.** Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment is done per contrast over
  all proteins tested in that contrast. With about 1,100 instead of about 10,000
  proteins, the number of tests is much smaller, so adjusted p-values and the
  set of significant redistributions differ.
- **Normalisation and imputation** are estimated from the proteins in the data.
  With fewer proteins, the loess normalisation and the imputed values for
  missing measurements change slightly.

If the results of the full dataset are available in `data/` (they are not part
of the repository), the overlap is shown below.

```{r compare-full}
full_file <- "data/Proteome/06_0_diff_and_scaled_mobility_top_movements_median.csv"

if (file.exists(full_file)) {
  full_candidates <- readr::read_csv(full_file, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    filter(adj_pval < 0.05)

  key <- c("pg_protein_groups", "treatment", "movement")
  tibble(
    `significant in subset`            = nrow(candidates),
    `also significant in full dataset` = nrow(semi_join(candidates, full_candidates, by = key))
  ) %>%
    knitr::kable()
} else {
  cat("Results of the full dataset not found in data/; comparison skipped.\n")
}
```
